terra.problem: The junk-drawer receipt joke does not connect clearly to the annual reminder of sins.
Hebrews quotes the passage but does not say the words are from Psalm 40. The explanation incorrectly attributes that identification to the writer.
Papa comments on how he will tell the passage instead of explaining the verse.
The joke makes the writer's parenthetical note the target and assumes the baker was suspicious of it.
‘It covers everything’ goes beyond the passage, which says we have been sanctified through Christ's sacrifice.
The joke compares Christ's once-for-all sacrifice to a cookie batch.
The joke compares Christ sitting at God's right hand after His sacrifice to Papa finishing a batch.
The passage does not say the priests keep going back into the temple.
‘It's a seat, not a trek’ makes Christ sitting at God's right hand the subject of a joke.
Papa mentions his years in the dark without identifying the drawer, leaving his backstory unclear to a baker who does not know it.
The joke compares the lasting effect of Christ's offering to a cookie's staying power.
The explanation repeats the answer and the verse without explaining what the writer says.

‘Yearly remembering was the old way’ risks attributing the annual remembering to the Lord. The passage says the sacrifices were an annual reminder of sins, not that the Lord remembered them every year.
